Text: Eli Lilly on Wednesday said its experimental combination regimen showed greater weight loss than a high dose of its top-selling drug, tirzepatide, alone in a mid-stage trial on patients with obesity and Type 2 diabetes. The combo therapy met the study’s main goals in a population that typically struggles to lose weight. The results boost hopes that it could serve as an alternative blockbuster treatment option for people who didn’t respond to or see the results they wanted on the current GLP-1 products on the market. Author: KryptonResearch14
Text: $LLY Lilly put up Phase 1 data at ESMO Saturday for sofetabart mipitecan, its FRα-targeting ADC, plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer. Confirmed response rate 79.3% (23 of 29 measurable patients, 6 complete responses), disease control 100%. The cohort was heavily pretreated, median 3 prior regimens, and 67% had already had a PARP inhibitor. Response rate held at 79% or higher in both the PARPi-treated and PARPi-naïve groups, and across FRα expression levels. Published platinum re-challenge data in the post-PARPi setting sits at 41.9% (per Lilly's release). Median duration of response and median PFS were not reached yet. Three Phase 3 trials are already running under FRAmework-01, at a lower 3 mg/kg dose than the 4 mg/kg used here.

Author: topstockalerts
Text: Eli Lilly said its obesity pill Foundayo significantly reduced the severity of obstructive sleep apnea, the most common sleep-related breathing disorder, in patients with obesity, in a late-stage trial. The drugmaker plans to file by the end of the year for U.S. approval of the daily pill for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, or OSA, in adults with obesity or who are overweight. The results make the pill — which rolled out in the U.S. in April — one of several GLP-1 treatments to show promise in treating the condition. OSA refers to interrupted breathing during sleep due to narrowed or blocked airways, which can cause drops in oxygen and increases in blood pressure that are associated with serious complications, such as hypertension, heart failure and stroke. The condition affects nearly 1 billion globally, including 80 million people ages 20 and over in the U.S., according to the National Council on Aging. Most have never been diagnosed, Lilly said in a release. $LLY

Author: topstockalerts
Text: The FDA will require manufacturers of GLP-1 drugs, including Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, to add safety warnings to their obesity and diabetes treatments regarding a rare eye condition called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), which can cause permanent vision loss. The decision follows a review of adverse-event reports and a meta-analysis of 126 clinical trials involving more than 134,000 patients. Researchers identified 6.4 NAION cases per 100,000 patient-years among GLP-1 users, compared with 3.8 cases in control groups. A separate FDA Sentinel study found a 43% higher risk compared with DPP-4 inhibitors, although no statistically significant difference was found versus SGLT-2 inhibitors. The warning adds to growing clinical and legal scrutiny surrounding semaglutide and tirzepatide. $NVO $LLY
